tasks.short: Advise on classification and salary complaints using job evidence, pay rules and employee discussions.

steps.what: Receive the complaint and clarify the requested outcome.
Retrieve job profiles, pay history and applicable classification rules.
Compare disputed duties and salary treatment with documented criteria and relevant precedents.

loop.input: Access-filtered complaint evidence pack and approved precedents.
loop.output: Criterion-by-criterion comparison with quotations, references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check source references and figures automatically; specialist verifies relevance and missing evidence.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; unresolved comparisons return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Descriptions of actual duties and complaint narratives require contextual reading.

steps.what: Discuss actual duties, disputed facts and concerns with the employee and manager.
Form a recommendation explaining classification, salary treatment and possible remedies.
Approve the advice and any proposed remedy within delegated authority.
Record the approved advice, evidence references and follow-up responsibility.
Send the approved written advice to the agreed recipients.

tasks.design: Configure restricted complaint intake in the {WORKFLOW} and retrieve evidence from the {HCM}, {PAYROLL} and {DOCS}. A bounded reading loop drafts a referenced comparison; specialists conduct discussions and formulate advice, while the HR manager approves the response. The {WORKFLOW} records and sends that exact approved version through the {HCM} and {EMAIL}, without changing pay.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence spans several systems, and similar job titles can conceal materially different duties. Rules alone cannot resolve contested facts or fairness concerns.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and integrations can assemble case packs. Bounded text extraction can prepare comparisons from approved sources.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed duties, inconsistent precedents and interpretation of collective agreements require expert judgement. GDPR, EU AI Act applicability and national rules require assessment before using models in employment decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Listen without prejudging the complaint, establish credible facts and explain a defensible recommendation.
tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time locating evidence and more time discussing disputed duties. They can offer early classification consultations within the approved framework; pay and grade changes require existing delegated approvals.

reach.learn: Collective-agreement interpretation, representation rights and escalation procedures.

reach.task: Check the implementation of an approved salary correction.
reach.learn: Effective dates, retrospective calculations and payroll cutoffs.

evidence.claim: Restricted case intake, evidence retrieval and approved-response routing are established deterministic patterns; this design is an estimate.
The human decision boundary reflects the potential significant effects of salary decisions; Article 22 applicability depends on the actual process.
Model use in worker evaluation or employment decisions needs an intended-use assessment against the EU AI Act.

assumptions: The baseline describes a typical mid-size employer; time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
Salary and classification advice remains a substantive human judgement despite the task's automation prior.
Consent and access work includes privacy review, access approval and employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Where complaint records and precedents are held today.
Which classification framework and collective agreements apply.
Who can approve advice, remedies and salary changes.
Whether permitted interfaces expose historical pay and job records.
research_questions: Which national complaint, representation and consultation rules apply?
Does the proposed model use fall within regulated employment AI?
How reliably can evidence extraction distinguish actual duties from job-title assumptions?
new_work: Verify extracted comparisons and irrelevant precedents.
Resolve missing records and conflicting effective dates.
Maintain access filters, retention rules and approved precedent versions.
Check that sent advice matches the approved version.

tasks.short: Prepare, negotiate and document collective agreements or mediated settlements within an approved mandate.

steps.what: Gather existing agreements, claims, grievances and workforce facts.
Calculate the cost and workforce effects of proposed terms.
Develop negotiating priorities, settlement options and proposed limits.
Approve bargaining limits and escalation conditions.
Negotiate terms or mediate grievances with the parties.
Draft agreement wording from the provisional settlement terms.

loop.input: Human-confirmed provisional terms, current agreement and approved clauses.
loop.output: Tracked agreement draft with a source for each changed clause.
loop.check: Compare amounts and dates deterministically; negotiator checks fidelity before legal review.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; ambiguities return to the negotiator without invented terms.
loop.why_not_simpler: Settlements combine existing clauses with negotiated wording that varies between cases.

steps.what: Review legal effect, consistency and implementation requirements.
Complete required ratification and sign the agreed settlement.
Archive the signed agreement and assign implementation actions.

tasks.design: Use the {DATA_PLATFORM} to assemble permitted workforce data and calculate bargaining scenarios from explicit assumptions. A bounded drafting loop in the {DOCS} converts human-confirmed terms into a tracked agreement for negotiator and legal review. Configure the {WORKFLOW}, {ESIGN} and {PROJECT} to track approvals, signatures and implementation actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Negotiation depends on trust, concessions and authority. Preparation is fragmented, and small wording differences can change an agreement's effect.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable scenario calculations and configured approval flows reduce preparation work. Bounded drafting can reconcile approved clauses with confirmed settlement notes.
tasks.still_hard: Bargaining power, credibility, ratification and mediation remain human responsibilities. National rules determine representation, consultation and enforceability; GDPR applies to sensitive grievance and union-related information.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room, earn trust, identify acceptable trade-offs and distinguish advocacy from impartial mediation.

ambition.what: Costed settlement-option review between bargaining rounds

tasks.altitude: During bargaining periods, the specialist can provide costed options between meetings and spend more time on trade-offs. Negotiating authority follows the approved mandate and existing ratification rights.

reach.task: Assess affordability of negotiated pay and benefit changes.
reach.learn: Scenario assumptions, total employment costs and budget sensitivity.
Mediation neutrality, caucus confidentiality and settlement authority.

evidence.claim: Deterministic costing, agreement versioning and approval routing can support human-led bargaining.
The digest supports retaining bargaining as human work while improving preparation and paperwork; it provides no bargaining automation case.
Employee-data consultation requirements vary nationally; the digest documents specific works council rights in the Netherlands.

assumptions: This is a composite workflow; mediation and collective bargaining may follow different routes.
The specialist supports an authorised negotiator or acts under an explicit mandate.
Time shares describe an active case or bargaining cycle, not a typical calendar week.
Consent and access ranges include confidential-data access and required employee consultation; statutory procedures may take longer.
unknowns: Whether the specialist represents a party or serves as a mediator.
Which agreement, mandate and ratification procedures apply.
Whether approved clauses and reliable costing assumptions exist.
Which preparation records can be shared with each party.
research_questions: Which national rules govern bargaining, mediation confidentiality and ratification?
What data may lawfully be used for workforce-level bargaining analysis?
Which scenario assumptions materially change settlement affordability?
new_work: Maintain cost assumptions and validate scenario calculations.
Confirm settlement notes before generating wording.
Review clause changes and unresolved ambiguities.
Track implementation actions and preserve confidential access boundaries.

tasks.short: Analyze workforce, occupation and industry data and communicate decision-ready technical findings.

steps.what: Agree the business question, population, measures and intended audience.
Retrieve workforce records, pay data and permitted occupational and industry datasets.
Reconcile definitions, job families, effective dates and missing values.
Calculate agreed measures and compare workforce groups and external benchmarks.
Interpret differences, test alternative explanations and identify decision implications.
Prepare the technical report with methods, findings, limitations and recommendations.

loop.input: Validated findings, calculated tables, approved methods and audience requirements.
loop.output: Report narrative linked to finding identifiers and deterministic tables.
loop.check: Verify numerical references automatically; specialist checks meaning, limitations and unsupported causal claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; unsupported passages are flagged for human writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Audience-specific explanations vary with the findings; calculations and table production remain deterministic.

steps.what: Approve the report and disclosure scope for its intended recipients.
Distribute the approved report and retain its source and version record.

tasks.design: Scheduled jobs in the {DATA_PLATFORM} join permitted extracts from the {HCM}, {PAYROLL} and reference datasets, validate definitions and feed the {BI}. Deterministic calculations produce tables, and a bounded loop drafts prose from findings already validated by the specialist. The {WORKFLOW} routes the report for disclosure approval before the {EMAIL} distributes the approved version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated extracts and reconciliations consume time, while inconsistent job definitions make comparisons unreliable. Interpretation requires business context that raw data does not contain.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable data mappings, validation rules and report templates can be built and maintained with less implementation effort. Models can draft explanations without calculating figures or choosing conclusions.
tasks.still_hard: External benchmarks may use incompatible populations or restricted licences. Small groups can expose employees, and observed differences do not establish causes.
tasks.human_edge: Choose meaningful comparisons, challenge misleading findings and explain what the evidence can support.
tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time interpreting trends and advising workforce decisions. They can prioritise recurring analyses within an agreed brief and bring evidence to monthly capacity reviews.

reach.learn: Capacity assumptions, business constraints and the distinction between correlation and causation.

reach.task: Investigate unexplained differences between employee groups.
reach.learn: Appropriate comparators, confidentiality and fair investigation methods.

evidence.claim: Workforce data reconciliation, reproducible calculations and scheduled reporting are established deterministic patterns.
The cited report failure supports checking generated prose against sources; it does not establish accuracy for this proposed workflow.
Consultation requirements for HR-data systems depend on national rules; the digest documents a Netherlands example.

assumptions: The baseline uses system extracts with reconciliation in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Recurring measures can be specified explicitly; interpretation remains expert work.
External distribution occurs only for requests with an approved purpose and recipient list.
Consent and access estimates include dataset licences, privacy review and required consultation.
unknowns: Which analytical questions recur and who uses the results.
Whether identifiers, job families and historical effective dates reconcile.
Which external datasets are licensed and available.
What disclosure thresholds and approval rights the organisation uses.
research_questions: Which benchmark definitions permit valid comparison across industries and occupations?
Which disclosure methods best protect small employee groups?
Does the proposed analysis constitute employee monitoring or otherwise require a DPIA?
new_work: Resolve data quality exceptions and maintain mappings.
Review benchmark coverage and licence changes.
Validate narrative claims against approved findings.
Maintain disclosure rules and refresh access permissions.

tasks.short: Assess job-analysis needs and develop, pilot and release suitable questionnaires, interview guides and observation materials.

steps.what: Clarify the analysis purpose, target roles and intended decisions.
Review existing instruments and identify coverage gaps.

loop.input: Approved existing instruments, requested scope and classification framework.
loop.output: Coverage matrix linking existing questions to required dimensions and identifying gaps.
loop.check: Require a source reference for every mapping; specialist checks coverage and ambiguous questions.
loop.stop: One mapping pass and one repair; uncertain mappings remain explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Questions express similar concepts in different language, requiring semantic comparison.

steps.what: Select analysis dimensions, response scales, sampling and collection methods.
Draft questionnaires, interview guides, observation sheets and participant instructions.

loop.input: Approved specification, reusable questions, response scales and instrument template.
loop.output: Draft instrument with each question linked to an approved analysis dimension.
loop.check: Validate required fields and scale consistency; specialist checks neutrality, accessibility and relevance.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; unresolved wording returns to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Novel roles need tailored wording beyond the approved reusable question library.

steps.what: Pilot the materials with jobholders and managers to test understanding and coverage.
Revise unclear items and document the instrument's limits.
Approve the instrument for its stated use and population.
Publish the approved materials and configure collection fields and access.

tasks.design: Keep approved questions, scales and templates in the {DOCS}, with versioned specifications and validation notes. Bounded loops compare coverage and draft only the tailored wording, while specialists choose methods, pilot materials and resolve feedback. Configure the {WORKFLOW} to publish the approved instrument as a controlled collection form.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each exercise reuses some materials but needs different wording and coverage. Copying templates is easy; establishing that questions capture the intended job demands is harder.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured specifications and reusable question libraries support deterministic assembly. Small model loops can compare wording and draft gaps for expert review.
tasks.still_hard: A polished questionnaire is not proof of validity. Representative sampling, gender-neutral evaluation, accessibility and local interpretation need specialist assessment; collection and later use must meet GDPR, EU AI Act and national requirements.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish real job demands from status claims and detect questions that systematically miss certain kinds of work.

ambition.what: Accessible job-analysis interviews for shift-based employees

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time testing whether instruments reflect actual work and less time assembling documents. They can choose suitable collection methods within the approved methodology and propose accessible alternatives for shift-based employees.

reach.task: Translate job demands into a skills-needs assessment.
reach.learn: Competency definitions and the distinction between role requirements and individual development needs.

reach.task: Review evaluation criteria for unequal treatment.
reach.learn: Gender-neutral criteria, accessibility and testing for systematic omissions.

evidence.claim: Reusable question libraries, versioned forms and template assembly are established techniques; the proposed semantic loops require local validation.
The digest identifies gender-neutral job evaluation as relevant to pay transparency; this does not validate any particular instrument.
Later use of AI outputs in worker evaluation needs separate assessment; document drafting alone does not establish the classification.

assumptions: The employer has an approved job-analysis methodology or will establish one before release.
Existing form configuration can represent the required scales and access controls.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot; broader validation or translation may take longer.
Consent and access work includes participant arrangements, privacy review and consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Which instruments, scales and question libraries already exist.
Which employee groups, languages and accessibility needs must be covered.
Whether outputs inform job descriptions, pay classification or individual evaluation.
Who approves methodology and whether representative pilot participants are available.
research_questions: Which validation methods suit the instrument's intended decisions?
How should pilot sampling cover shift patterns and less visible work?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the collection method and subsequent use?
new_work: Review generated questions and their dimension mappings.
Maintain approved question versions and retire unsuitable items.
Organise representative pilots and resolve inconsistent interpretations.
Monitor instrument use beyond its validated scope.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward evidence quality, fair methodology, difficult discussions and interpretation. Specialists gain room to propose recurring reviews and accessible services within approved mandates; formal pay, bargaining and disclosure rights follow delegated authority.
reach: Support labor relations specialists with costed options and referenced grievance evidence.
Help human resources managers connect workforce findings to planning decisions.
Work with equal opportunity officers on fair criteria and defensible comparisons.
Help payroll teams implement approved changes with clear effective dates.
skills_to_grow: Privacy, access control and employment-AI intended-use assessment.
Mediation, employee consultation and clear explanations of difficult decisions.
role.ambitious_version: A specialist who brings reliable evidence into workforce decisions more frequently, offers early classification clarification and makes job analysis accessible to employee groups that standard forms underserve.

job.title: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
